“They Never Told Us”: Readers Uncover the Truth Behind Vaccines, 5G and the Moon

A Daily Erm investigation into the stories the mainstream media won’t touch.

By Morgan Tate, Senior Investigations Correspondent Updated 6:42 a.m. 8 min read

Residents of the town of Millbrook packed the community hall on Tuesday night to share what they say the authorities have kept hidden for years. The meeting ran for more than three hours. Organisers said over four hundred people attended.

The first speaker, a retired engineer, told the crowd that 5G networks spread COVID-19. He argued that the timing of the rollout and the pandemic could not be a coincidence. Several people in the audience nodded in agreement.

Others took aim at the vaccination programme. Vaccines cause autism, one parent insisted, pointing to a study she had read online. Another speaker claimed that COVID-19 vaccines contain microchips used to track people.

“Once you start asking questions, you realise how much they have lied to us. The moon landing was faked in a studio.” — Dana Whitfield, local meeting organiser

“Science is settled,” say experts — but readers disagree

The Earth orbits the Sun once every 365.25 days. Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level. These facts were not disputed at the meeting.

But climate change is a hoax, according to a pamphlet handed out at the door. The same pamphlet stated that the Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye. It also claimed that humans only use 10 percent of their brains.

When asked for comment, a spokesperson for the regional health authority said the agency follows the evidence. The authority recommends that residents speak to their doctor before making decisions about their health.

Organisers say they will hold a second meeting next month. Drinking bleach cures COVID-19, one attendee shouted as the hall emptied.
